Sewer Pipe Trap.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:32] (expert) on the floor panels before the plate falls away
Sewer Pipe Trap.hazarddescription: Pressure-sensitive panels in the floor connects to a metal plate holding a number of sewer pipes shut in the ceiling.

Filth Fall.name: Filth Fall
Filth Fall.description:
Trigger Pressure is placed on the floor tiles

Effect The metal plate above gives way, unleashing a torrent of sewage and flesh-eating worms on everyone within 10 feet of the pressure plate. Anyone hit by the filth must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} and takes @Damage[2d12[piercing]] damage.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} and takes @Damage[4d12[piercing]] damage.

Critical Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 4} and takes @Damage[4d12[piercing]] damage plus @Damage[2d12[persistent,piercing]] damage.

Quick Capture.description:
Trigger A creature hits or touches the flytrap.

Effect The flytrap makes a leaf Strike against the triggering creature. If it hits, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in that leaf.
Quick Capture.name: Quick Capture

Hungry Flurry.name: Hungry Flurry
Hungry Flurry.description: The flytrap makes four leaf Strikes at a -2 penalty, each against a different target. These attacks count toward the flytrap's multiple attack penalty, but the multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after it makes all its attacks.

Focused Assault.name: Focused Assault
Focused Assault.description: The flytrap attacks a single target with all four of its leaves. The flytrap makes one leaf Strike. On a success, the flytrap deals the damage from one leaf Strike plus an additional [[/r {1d8}]]{1d8 damage} for every leaf beyond the first. On a failure, the flytrap deals the damage from one leaf Strike, but it can't use Improved Grab. It deals no damage on a critical failure. This counts toward the flytrap's multiple attack penalty as a number of attacks equal to the number of leaves the flytrap has.

Greater Infestation.name: Greater Infestation
Greater Infestation.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:29]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[2d8[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[3d8[persistent,poison]] damage and can hear root rotter thoughts within 30 feet as an imprecise sense (2 rounds)

Stage 3 as stage 2, but @Damage[4d8[persistent,poison]] damage and arise as a root rotter upon death (2 rounds).

This replaces the Grab and Swallow Whole abilities possessed by giant flytraps.

Fungal Flytrap.name: Fungal Flytrap
Fungal Flytrap.publicNotes:
Because they blend in so well with surrounding foliage, giant flytraps can use the element of surprise to make quick strikes against unsuspecting adventurers and forest travelers.

Flytraps eagerly feed on humanoids, monstrous insects, and larger prey.

Shadow Spawn.name: Shadow Spawn
Shadow Spawn.description: When a creature's shadow is pulled free by Steal Shadow, it becomes a shadow spawn under the command of the shadow that created it. This @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.pathfinder-monster-core.Actor.clzHAfegb9Rn6DOe]{Shadow Spawn} doesn't have Steal Shadow. If the creature the shadow spawn was pulled from dies, the shadow spawn becomes a full-fledged, autonomous shadow. If the creature recovers from its enfeeblement, its shadow returns to it and the shadow spawn is extinguished.

Slink in Shadows.name: Slink in Shadows
Slink in Shadows.description: The shadow can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.XMcnh4cSI32tljXa]{Hide} or end its @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.VMozDqMMuK5kpoX4]{Sneak} in a creature's or object's shadow.

Light Vulnerability.name: Light Vulnerability
Light Vulnerability.description: Attacks against the shadow are treated as magical if made by a creature who is in magical light or with an object that is in magical light (such as from the @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.WBmvzNDfpwka3qT4]{Light} spell).

Steal Shadow.name: Steal Shadow
Steal Shadow.description:
Requirements The shadow hit a living creature with a shadow hand Strike on its previous action

Effect The shadow pulls at the target's shadow, making the creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 3} on a critical hit). This is cumulative with other enfeebled conditions from shadows, to a maximum of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 4}. If this increases a creature's enfeebled value to 3 or more, the target's shadow is separated from its body (see shadow spawn). The enfeebled value from @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.RDXXE7wMrSPCLv5k]{Steal} Shadow decreases by 1 every hour.

Greater Shadow.name: Greater Shadow
Greater Shadow.publicNotes:
Shadows that spend long amounts of time on the Netherworld and absorb its magic become greater shadows.

The mysterious undead known as shadows lurk in dark places and feed on those who stray too far from the light.

Greftan Hinash.name: Greftan Hinash
Greftan Hinash.publicNotes:
Saboteurs excel at infiltration, using it to perform destructive acts, whether they are the physical destruction of a valuable object or obstructing important political proceedings. Unlike those of spies, the motivations of saboteurs is not to steal information, but rather to sow chaos among their enemies.

Villains pursue selfish and cruel goals, trampling over anyone foolish or purehearted enough to stand in their way.

Snare Crafting.name: Snare Crafting
Snare Crafting.description: The saboteur can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.rmwa3OyhTZ2i2AHl]{Craft} snares and has the supplies to make up to two @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.kF761P3ibBIFmLm9]{Caltrop Snares} and up to two @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.Km4lSOsyrip5q6iD]{Hampering Snares}.

+2 status to reflex saves vs. traps.name: +2 status to reflex saves vs. traps

+2 status to perception to find traps.name: +2 status to perception to find traps

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The saboteur deals an extra 1d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Veil of Lies.name: Veil of Lies
Veil of Lies.description:
15 feet. A degholau exudes a faint scent of rotting wildflowers in its aura—an odor that dulls the mind. A creature that ends its turn in the aura must attempt a @Check[will|dc:30] save.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected and is temporarily immune to Veil of Lies for 1 minute.

Success The creature is unaffected.

Failure The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} while it remains in the aura and for 10 minutes after leaving the aura.

Critical Failure As failure, except @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2}.

Conspiratorial Thoughts.name: Conspiratorial Thoughts
Conspiratorial Thoughts.description:
Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:33]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (1 round)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 2} (1 round)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.9qGBRpbX9NEwtAAr]{Controlled} by the degholau (1 round)

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Exposure Vulnerability.name: Exposure Vulnerability
Exposure Vulnerability.description: The first time each round that a creature critically succeeds at a save against a degholau's Veil of Lies or that a creature confronts the fiend on a falsehood immediately after the demon fails to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.ewwCglB7XOPLUz72]{Lie}, the degholau takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Degholau.name: Degholau
Degholau.publicNotes:
Degholaus form from wretched souls who betrayed their societies to evil ends or for personal gain. These fiends resemble bloated, bestial humanoids with eyeless mole-like faces. They have five tails, all of which feature blood-red eyes.

High Crimes

Those whose souls become degholaus abused positions of authority in their nation for personal gain or simply out of a need for cruelty. They might have sold secrets, weakened institutions, or initiated military action against their own people. Some initially deluded themselves into believing their actions were righteous or victimless, but eventually embraced their destructive role, damaging their soul so completely they transform into these demons after their judgment.

equipment-Scroll of Heal (Rank 7).name: Scroll of Heal (Rank 7)
equipment-Scroll of Heal (Rank 7).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}

Casting a Spell from a scroll requires holding the scroll in one hand and activating it with a Cast a Spell activity using the normal number of actions for that spell.

The spell must appear on your spell list. Because you're the one Casting the Spell, use your spell attack modifier and spell DC. The spell also gains the appropriate trait for your tradition (arcane, divine, occult, or primal).

Any physical costs are provided when a scroll is created, so you don't need to provide them when casting from a scroll. If the spell requires a locus, you must have that locus to Cast the Spell from a scroll.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Desperation Vulnerability.name: Desperation Vulnerability
Desperation Vulnerability.description: Sinmolds are aware that they're in a vulnerable state as formless "newborn fiends" and are desperate to become stronger before they become prey to more powerful demons. Whenever the sinmold is in a combat encounter and ends its turn without dealing damage to another creature, the sinmold takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Digestion.name: Digestion
Digestion.description: The first time in a round when the sinmold damages a creature with Engulf, the sinmold immediately restores Hit Points equal to the damage dealt, gaining Hit Points in excess of its maximum as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. As long as the sinmold possesses these temporary Hit Points, its surface hardens, and its AC increases to 30.

Sinmold Infestation.name: Sinmold Infestation
Sinmold Infestation.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[2d8[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[3d8[poison]] damage and can hear the thoughts of root rotters within 30 feet as an imprecise sense (1 round)

Stage 3 as stage 2, but @Damage[4d8[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (1 round)

Stage 4 as stage 3, and arise as a root rotter upon death (1 round)

equipment-Countering Charm (Toxic Cloud).name: Countering Charm (Toxic Cloud)
equipment-Countering Charm (Toxic Cloud).description:
This glittering charm is made of a gemstone flawed with a leaden inclusion. Spellcasters can cast spells into countering charms that they've invested or that are invested by a willing creature. The spell's effect doesn't occur; the spell's power is instead stored within the charm, replacing any spell previously there. The charm can hold only spells cast from spell slots, not cantrips or focus spells. While the charm is invested, the creature who has invested it knows what spell is stored within and automatically identifies that spell when it's cast.

Activate—Counter R (manipulate)

Trigger You are targeted by or within the area of the spell stored within the charm

Requirements You have a free hand

Effect You present the charm and attempt to counteract the triggering spell, using the rank of the spell stored in the charm and a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+20 #Counteract]]{+20}. This expends the spell held in the charm.

equipment-Wand of Sending (Rank 5).name: Wand of Sending (Rank 5)
equipment-Wand of Sending (Rank 5).description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.R9xqCBblkS5KE4y7]{Sending}

This baton is about a foot long and contains a single spell. The appearance typically relates to the spell within.

Activate Cast a Spell

Frequency once per day, plus overcharge

Effect You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank.

Craft Requirements Supply a casting of the spell at the listed rank.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Shattering Blow.name: Shattering Blow
Shattering Blow.description: Lukarazyll slams his fists into the ground, shattering the terrain around him. Creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] from Lukarazyll take @Damage[4d12[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:32|basic] save). Those who fail are knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. In addition, all squares within 15 feet of Lukarazyll become difficult terrain.

Spore Burst.name: Spore Burst
Spore Burst.description: Whenever Lukarazyll picks up debris to throw, tendrils of fungus burrow out from his hands, infesting the debris so that when it hits, it explodes into a cloud of toxic spores. All non-fungus creatures in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:10] (including the target) must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save. The target of the debris takes a –2 circumstance penalty to this save. Those that fail take @Damage[2d6[persistent,poison]] damage and are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1}. Creatures can't remove the sickened condition while this persistent damage remains.

Mirror Vulnerability.name: Mirror Vulnerability
Mirror Vulnerability.description: Lukarazyll, like all abrikandilu, despises the sight of his own reflection. When a creature Interacts with a mirror within sight of Lukarazyll, he takes a –2 penalty to Will saves against fear effects. If he ends his turn adjacent to a mirror, or the first time in a round he's attacked by a creature holding a mirror, Lukarazyll takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage.

Loathsome Bite.name: Loathsome Bite
Loathsome Bite.description:
When Lukarazyll hits a creature with his jaws Strike, the creature becomes infected with the demon's self-loathing. The creature must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:34] save to avoid gaining a –1 status penalty to Charisma-based checks. This penalty is cumulative up to –3, and remains even if the wounds are healed. The penalty is reduced by 1 every 24 hours until it reaches 0.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.LgZx5xotO08JzhVc]{Effect: Mutilating Bite}

Wreck.name: Wreck
Wreck.description: Lukarazyll makes two claw Strikes against an unattended object, wrenching and gouging it while infesting it with tendrils of fungus. If both Strikes hit, combine their damage for the purpose of overcoming its Hardness. These Strikes don't count toward Lukarazyll's multiple attack penalty, nor does that penalty apply to these strikes. If the object is destroyed, Lukarazyll can use it as hurled debris—the remnants automatically become fungus-infested as part of this act and can create a spore burst on a successful hit.

Lukarazyll.name: Lukarazyll
Lukarazyll.publicNotes:
Wrecker demons, also known as abrikandilus, despise beautiful things and do everything in their power to destroy both people and objects regarded as such. An abrikandilu forms from the souls mortals who were vandals, misanthropes, or defacers of artwork, particularly if their destructive actions stemmed from feelings of powerful envy.

An abrikandilu loathes only one thing more than beauty: their own visage. The mere sight of their face-reflected in a mirror, a shield, or even a pool of water- can send a wrecker demon into a rage. Many demon slayers leverage tactic to their advantage, venturing into battle with polished steel shields and cold iron blades at the ready.

Mortal souls that have been twisted and corrupted by sin sometimes arise in the afterlife as demons. These powerful and destructive fiends seek to spread their particular sin to warp more souls, thereby bolstering their numbers and continuing the cycle.

equipment-Wand of Howling Blizzard (Rank.name: Wand of Howling Blizzard (Rank 5)
equipment-Wand of Howling Blizzard (Rank.description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xxWhyl81w3ckslAU]{Howling Blizzard}

This baton is about a foot long and contains a single spell. The appearance typically relates to the spell within.

Activate Cast a Spell

Frequency once per day, plus overcharge

Effect You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank.

Craft Requirements Supply a casting of the spell at the listed rank.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Limber.description: A grizzer ignores difficult terrain from narrow confines and can move at full Speed when Squeezing.
Limber.name: Limber

Regurgitate.name: Regurgitate
Regurgitate.description: The grizzer regurgitates a creature or unattended item from their stomach into an adjacent unoccupied space.

Cold Iron Indigestion.name: Cold Iron Indigestion
Cold Iron Indigestion.description: If the grizzer swallows a cold iron item or a creature holding or wearing a cold iron item, the grizzer becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until they regurgitate it.

Extradimensional Stomach.name: Extradimensional Stomach
Extradimensional Stomach.description: The grizzer's stomach is an extradimensional space (that appears to be an immense elongated leathery chamber) capable of holding up to 24 Bulk. Unless the grizzer uses Digest, the space has the same environment as the grizzer's surroundings, and creatures inside don't take damage from being swallowed, nor do they face the threat of suffocation.

Digest.name: Digest
Digest.description: The grizzer fills their stomach with acid for 1 round to digest its contents. Creatures inside the stomach must hold their breath or start suffocating, and they take @Damage[4d8[acid]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic] save). The grizzer can Sustain this activity, in which case the stomach remains filled with acid; creatures inside take acid damage at the end of their turn and can't catch their breath. The grizzer regains 10 Hit Points if at least one creature takes acid damage as a result of Digest.

Snatch Object.name: Snatch Object
Snatch Object.description: The grizzer unfurls their sticky tongue at a creature within 15 feet and attempts to either pull the target closer or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} it. If they choose to pull the target, they attempt an Athletics check against the target's Fortitude DC and pull it into an adjacent space on a success. If the grizzer attempts to Disarm the target, they gain a +1 circumstance bonus to the Athletics check if the item is made of shiny material or magically illuminated, such as by revealing light. If the Disarm attempt critically succeeds, the grizzer also grabs the item with their tongue and swallows it.

Grizzer.name: Grizzer
Grizzer.publicNotes:
These gangly fey lizards are known for two traits. First, they look ridiculous when they run, dashing on hind legs while waving their front legs wildly in the air. Second, they're inveterate thieves with the ability to store an extraordinary amount of goods in their stomach. Many grizzers appeared in the River Kingdoms a little over 10 years ago, but several coordinated hunts drove them further southwest, where they've begun to thrive in the forests of Razmiran.

Strange Fey Appetites

A grizzer's strange appetite isn't unique among fey. Azarpals, for example, can store food in their bellies and infuse them with poisons that wreak havoc on feasts and banquets. Stories of whales swimming in otherworldly seas that have swallowed entire villages, or of duplicitous serpentine fey who can assume the forms of those they consume, suggest that fey with strange appetites aren't so unusual on the First World.

Sacrilegious Aura.name: Sacrilegious Aura
Sacrilegious Aura.description: 30 feet. When a creature in the aura uses a vitality spell or ability, the graveknight automatically attempts to counteract it, with a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+18 #Counteract]]{+18}.

Weapon Master.description: The graveknight has access to the critical specialization effects of any weapons it wields.
Weapon Master.name: Weapon Master

Dragon Bonded.name: Dragon Bonded
Dragon Bonded.description: Captain Talymir is immune to Ulugurnix's frightful presence aura, Poison Breath, and stench aura. If Ulugurnix is destroyed, Captain Talymir becomes infuriated. He deals 2 additional damage on melee Strikes and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} for 3 rounds; he can use the extra action to Stride or Strike.

Devastating Blast.name: Devastating Blast
Devastating Blast.description: The graveknight unleashes a @Template[cone|distance:30] of energy. Creatures in the area take @Damage[12d6[cold]] with a @Check[reflex|dc:30|basic]. The graveknight can use this ability once every [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge devastating blast]] rounds.

Graveknight's Curse.name: Graveknight's Curse
Graveknight's Curse.description:
This curse affects anyone who wears a graveknight's armor for at least 1 hour

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:34] save

Onset 1 hour

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 2}, –10-foot status penalty to Speeds, and can't remove armor (1 day)

Stage 3 dies and transforms into the armor's graveknight.

Captain Talymir.name: Captain Talymir
Captain Talymir.publicNotes: Graveknights are undead warriors granted unlife by a cursed suit of armor.

equipment-Razmir Robes and Masks.name: Razmir Robes and Masks
equipment-Razmir Robes and Masks.description: The robes and masks here are authentic and would grant a +2 circumstance bonus on Deception checks to Impersonate a member of Razmir’s faith.

Chalzo Rove.name: Chalzo Rove
Chalzo Rove.blurb: Druman diplomat seeking to profit from conflict
Chalzo Rove.publicNotes: Chalzo Rove is a middle-aged woman wearing the traditional white robes of the Kalistocracy along with matching long white gloves. She wears a good deal of gold jewelry featuring a variety of perfect gems. The skin of her face (the only skin visible) is flawless and flushed, and her dark brown hair is immaculately kept.

Root Rotter.name: Root Rotter

Fungus Sense.name: Fungus Sense
Fungus Sense.description: A root rotter has imprecise tremorsense to detect the vibrations of creatures who are within a region of fungal terrain shared by the root rotter.

Fungal Empowerment.name: Fungal Empowerment
Fungal Empowerment.description: If the root rotter is touching fungal terrain at the start of its turn, they regain @Damage[10[healing]] Hit Points and are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} that turn; they can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.

Fungal Mind.name: Fungal Mind
Fungal Mind.description: Root rotters communicate telepathically with each other. While within telepathic range of at least one other root rotter, they gain a +2 circumstance bonus to initiative rolls, Perception checks, and saving throws against mental effects. If one root rotter is aware of a combatant, all members of the fungal mind within range are aware of it.

Fungal Root.name: Fungal Root
Fungal Root.description:
Requirements The root rotter is standing in fungal terrain

Effect Fungal roots reach out to snag a nearby foe. An enemy within 30 feet of the root rotter takes @Damage[4d6[piercing]] damage and must attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:27] saving throw.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature takes half damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} until the end of its next turn.

Failure The creature takes full damage and becomes clumsy 1 with an unlimited duration. In addition, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained} (@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} DC 27) for 1 minute.

Critical Failure As failure but double damage. In addition, the creature is exposed to rotter infestation.

Rotter Infestation.name: Rotter Infestation
Rotter Infestation.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:27]

Onset 1 day

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 day)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} and can sense the presence of root rotters within 30 feet as an imprecise sense (1 round)

Stage 3 as stage 2, but transformation into a root rotter upon death (1 day)

Root Rotter.publicNotes:
Root rotters are all that remain of the unfortunate elven residents of Greengold. Some died in the initial bursts of Jeharlu spores, while others succumbed to infestation by sinmolds. Fungus now riddles their bodies, wrapping around their brains and nerves to reanimate them.

Corruption Spreaders

A root rotter that remains in place for 24 hours causes a @Template[type:emanation|distance:5] to become overgrown with foul-smelling unpleasant fungus. This spread increases by 5 feet for each additional 24 hours the root rotter remains motionless, to a maximum area of a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] after 12 days of motionless lurking. This fungus is permanent as long as it has a source of nourishment but can be destroyed as easily as any patch of mundane fungus.

Nimble Dodge.name: Nimble Dodge
Nimble Dodge.description:
Trigger The blade assassin is targeted with a melee or ranged attack by an attacker they can see

Effect The blade assassin gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack

Otherworldly Will.name: Otherworldly Will
Otherworldly Will.description: The blade assassin is driven forward by a singular, otherworldly will, guiding their actions. Whenever the blade assassin attempts a Will saving throw against a mental effect that would control or dictate their actions, the blade assassin treats the result of the saving throw as one category better.

Unexplained Demise.name: Unexplained Demise
Unexplained Demise.description:
Trigger The assassin is captured alive

Effect Blood pours from the assassin's ears and nose, and they drop dead on the spot. An adjacent PC who witnesses this unexplained death must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:22] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Poison Weapon.name: Poison Weapon
Poison Weapon.description:
Requirements The blade assassin is wielding a piercing or slashing weapon and has a free hand

Effect The blade assassin applies a poison to the weapon.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The blade assassin deals an extra 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the blade assassin.

Clavance Ordranti.name: Clavance Ordranti
Clavance Ordranti.blurb: Spoiled nobleman who doesn’t take life seriously
Clavance Ordranti.publicNotes: Clavance Ordranti is a well-dressed nobleman who appears to be in his mid-twenties. His skin is very pale, owing to his dhampir heritage, a bloodline he inherited from his mother and not something he speaks of openly.

Fungal Heart.stealthdetails: (master) to detect that the fungal heart is hazardous; noticing the fungal heart has a DC of 0
Fungal Heart.name: Fungal Heart
Fungal Heart.disable: @Check[nature|dc:33] (master) three times to carefully prune away specific tethers that keep the fungal heart active, or @Check[religion|dc:33] (master) three times to exorcise the demonic energies from the fungal heart.
Fungal Heart.hazarddescription: A pulsing green cluster of fungus suspended in the middle of the spherical room by thick lengths of fibrous stalks.
Fungal Heart.routine: (1 action; divine, poison) The fungal heart clenches as if beating like a real heart, then exudes a churning cloud of toxic spores that fills areas D1 and D2. All creatures in these areas take @Damage[10d6[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:34|basic] save; creatures in area D1 gain a +4 circumstance bonus to this save due to the diffusion of the spores as they wash into the larger area).
Fungal Heart.reset: The fungal heart deactivates and resets if 3 rounds pass during which no attempts to disable or damage it take place. On subsequent activations of "Treerazer Notices," no telepathic message is sent—it's simply an overwhelming sensation of imminent doom.

Treerazer Notices.name: Treerazer Notices
Treerazer Notices.description:
Trigger The fungal heart takes damage, or an attempt to disable it fails

Effect A sinister voice fills the minds of all creatures in area D1 or D2, speaking in Chthonian: "And so my whelp has failed, yet you have not found salvation—you have doomed Kyonin to fall. Will you be the first to die, or shall you linger long enough to see all you hold dear become mine?" The PCs immediately recognize this voice as belonging to Treerazer and must attempt a @Check[will|dc:39] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 2} (or doomed 1, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 4}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.sDPxOjQ9kx2RZE8D]{Fleeing} for as long as they remain frightened on a critical failure). The Fungal Heart then rolls initiative.

Accept Tithe.name: Accept Tithe
Accept Tithe.description:
Trigger A creature drops or offers at least 750 gp in valuables within 15 feet of the tithekeeper

Effect The tithekeeper quickly uses its feet to scoop the valuables into its vault and is now indifferent toward the triggering creature unless that creature uses hostile actions against it or its allies.

Rip Off.name: Rip Off
Rip Off.description:
Requirements The tithekeeper has Impaled a creature

Effect The tithekeeper tears the creature loose from its spiky feet, releasing it. The creature takes @Damage[4d10[slashing]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:29|basic] save) and is no longer @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}. On a failed save, the creature also takes @Damage[2d8[persistent,bleed]] damage.

Eyes Behind the Mask.name: Eyes Behind the Mask
Eyes Behind the Mask.description: A creature wearing the mask and garb of a priest of Razmir that outranks the tithekeeper's mask and ribbon rank can spend an hour Interacting with the tithekeeper's mask to connect with it. The creature's mask becomes an invested item that allows them to see and hear as though peering through the tithekeeper's mask. The creature must use a 3-action activity envisioning the tithekeeper to activate the scrying effect, and the effect can be Dismissed. Multiple creatures can create connections to the tithekeeper's mask simultaneously, and a creature can have connections to multiple tithekeepers with just one mask. Each connection ends after a week but can be renewed at any time.

Capacity for Punishment.name: Capacity for Punishment
Capacity for Punishment.description: The tithekeeper can have up to six creatures impaled and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} with its feet at once.

Locked Vault.name: Locked Vault
Locked Vault.description: The tithekeeper's body is a locked vault containing any tithes given to it. The vault's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.2EE4aF4SZpYf0R6H]{Pick Lock} DC is 29 and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SjmKHgI7a5Z9JzBx]{Force Open} DC is 33.

Tithekeeper.name: Tithekeeper
Tithekeeper.publicNotes:
Razmir's most powerful priests deploy tithekeepers to ensure his followers don't develop sticky fingers. These ziggurat-like constructs have over two dozen legs and a trap-like mouth. At its top, a mask with a colored ribbon attached denotes its symbolic rank in the Church of Razmir.

Instruments of Terror

Though the tithekeeper's primary function is to collect coins, they're capable of great violence. Priests who determine a village is too far behind on payments might have their tithekeeper skewer multiple residents and wave its victims' bodies in the air as it parades through the streets. Those who survive the ordeal are highly motivated to avoid a repeat experience.

Aromina Yasgon.name: Aromina Yasgon
Aromina Yasgon.publicNotes: A middle aged human woman who dresses rather plainly for this important council, but her look is used primarily to put others at ease.

Enhanced Fireball Rune.name: Enhanced Fireball Rune
Enhanced Fireball Rune.disable: @Check[thievery|dc:32] (expert) to erase the rune without triggering the sensor, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9HpwDN4MYQJnW0LG]{Dispel Magic} (6th rank; counteract DC 27) to counteract the rune
Enhanced Fireball Rune.hazarddescription: An invisible rune creates an invisible, spherical magical sensor with a 20-foot radius.

Fireball.name: Fireball
Fireball.description:
Trigger A living creature enters the sensor area

Effect The rune detonates a fireball centered on the triggering creature's square. This is a 6th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.sxQZ6yqTn0czJxVd]{Fireball} spell that deals @Damage[12d6[fire]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:29|basic|traits:fire|options:item:spell] save).

Nalora.name: Nalora
Nalora.publicNotes: Dressed in revealing yellow silks and carrying a thorn-covered staff emitting a pale-yellow glow.

Spore Burst.description:
Trigger Vintalax takes damage from a melee Strike made by an adjacent creature

Effect Vintalax's corrupted body unleashes a cloud of spores that envelopes the attacker, quickly growing and dissolving their flesh. These spores deal @Damage[4d6[persistent,poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:34|basic] save).
Spore Burst.name: Spore Burst

Rotting Gift.name: Rotting Gift
Rotting Gift.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:34]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 1} (1 day)

Stage 2 stupefied 1 and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 1} (1 day)

Stage 3 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.e1XGnhKNSQIm5IXg]{Stupefied 2} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.4D2KBtexWXa6oUMR]{Drained 2} (1 day)

Stage 4 drained 1 and controlled by the Rotting God (1 day)

Stage 5 controlled by the Rotting God (1 day)

Stage 6 the creature becomes permanently controlled by the Rotting God (and may gain unique fungus-themed abilities)—at this point the creature is no longer diseased, and the control can only be ended by the death of the Rotting God or by an effect that removes curses. The creature loses any fungus-themed abilities granted by rotting gift as soon as it's removed.

Spore Breath.name: Spore Breath
Spore Breath.description: Vintalax unleashes a cloud of spores from his mouth in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30]. Creatures in this area take @Damage[12d6[acid]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:34|basic] save). Those who fail this save are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure) as the spores enter their lungs and begin to grow. These creatures take @Damage[2d6[persistent,bleed]] damage as long as they remain sickened. This bleed damage cannot be stopped as long as the sickened condition persists. Any creature that takes damage from spore breath is exposed to rotting gift.

Tentacle Eruption.name: Tentacle Eruption
Tentacle Eruption.description: Vintalax drives his tentacles into the ground, causing tendrils of fungus to erupt everywhere in area B9. This deals @Damage[2d8[bludgeoning],3d6[acid]]{2d8 bludgeoning damage plus 3d6 acid} damage to each creature in the area (@Check[reflex|dc:34|basic] save). Creatures that fail their save against tentacle eruption are grasped by the tendrils, reducing their speed by 10 feet until the start of Vintalax's next turn (or are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.eIcWbB5o3pP6OIMe]{Immobilized} on a critical failure).

Otherworldly Will.name: Otherworldly Will
Otherworldly Will.description: Vintalax is driven forward by a singular, otherworldly will, guiding their actions. Whenever Vintalax attempts a Will saving throw against a mental effect that would control or dictate their actions, Vintalax treats the result of the saving throw as one category better.

Throne Tethered.name: Throne Tethered
Throne Tethered.description: Vintalax is attached to his throne by a twisted length of thorny fungal vines that limit his mobility to areas B9 and B10. This tether can be destroyed (AC 30, Hardness 12, HP 50 (BT 25), Immunities acid, bludgeoning; Resistances piercing 10), in which case Vintalax howls in pain as his body rapidly begins to decay. Each round that he remains severed from the throne he loses his fast healing and takes @Damage[4d6[spirit]] damage at the start of his turn, but his AC increases to 36 and his speed to 25 feet, due to his increased mobility. He can end this effect by sitting back down on his throne (an Interact action) and remaining there until the end of his turn, at which point a new fungus tether reattaches to him.

equipment-Marvelous Medicines (Stored in.name: Marvelous Medicines (Stored in Retrieval Belt)
equipment-Marvelous Medicines (Stored in.description:
This healer's toolkit contains a seemingly endless supply of bandages, herbs, and healing items of impeccable quality, granting you a +2 item bonus to Medicine checks.

If you use the marvelous medicines when you @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.KjoCEEmPGTeFE4hh]{Treat Poison} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.TC7OcDa7JlWbqMaN]{Treat Disease}, before you roll your check, the medicines attempt to counteract the poison or disease you're treating, with a counteract rank of 5 and a counteract modifier of [[/r 1d20+21 #Counteract]]{+21}. This is a healing effect.

The medicines can't be used to treat the same affliction for that patient again

equipment-Healing Potion (Greater) (Stor.name: Healing Potion (Greater) (Stored in Retrieval Belt)
equipment-Healing Potion (Greater) (Stor.description:
Activate A (manipulate)

A healing potion is a vial of a ruby-red liquid that imparts a tingling sensation as the drinker's wounds heal rapidly. When you drink a healing potion, you regain @Damage[(6d8+20)[healing]] Hit Points.

equipment-Potion of Fire Resistance (Mod.name: Potion of Fire Resistance (Moderate) (Stored in Retrieval Belt)
equipment-Potion of Fire Resistance (Mod.description:
Activate A (manipulate)

Drinking this thick, fortifying potion grants resistance 10 against fire damage for 1 hour.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-effects.Item.8zKGaGrkTd8ALqJO]{Effect: Potion of Fire Resistance (Moderate)}

equipment-Wand of Lightning Bolt (Rank 5.name: Wand of Lightning Bolt (Rank 5) (Stored in Retrieval Belt)
equipment-Wand of Lightning Bolt (Rank 5.description:
@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.9AAkVUCwF6WVNNY2]{Lightning Bolt}

This baton is about a foot long and contains a single spell. The appearance typically relates to the spell within.

Activate Cast a Spell

Frequency once per day, plus overcharge

Effect You Cast the Spell at the indicated rank.

Craft Requirements Supply a casting of the spell at the listed rank.

Note: To create a scroll or wand of a specific spell, drag the spell from the compendium or compendium browser into the inventory of a PC, NPC, or loot actor.

Isqulugia.name: Isqulugia
Isqulugia.description:
Isqulugia's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed} conditions can't be removed until this affliction is removed

Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Stage 1 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (1 hour)

Stage 2 @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.HL2l2VRSaQHu9lUw]{Fatigued} and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} (1 day)

Stage 3 fatigued and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} (1 day)

Stage 4 paralyzed (1 day)

Stage 5 the creature dies, and its body violently transforms into a new isqulug. @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.6dDtGIUerazSHIOu]{Wish}, similar magic, or a 9th-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kqhPt9344UkcGVYO]{Resurrect} ritual can return the victim to life. The new isqulug remains even if the victim is brought back to life.

Swamp Stride.description: An isqulug ignores difficult terrain that's caused by typical features of swamps.
Swamp Stride.name: Swamp Stride

Host Scent.name: Host Scent
Host Scent.description: An isqulug can precisely sense any creature infected with isqulugia within 30 feet, and knows the current stage of the disease.

Spore Cloud.name: Spore Cloud
Spore Cloud.description:
Trigger The Tanglebriar isqulug is hit by a melee attack

Effect The Tanglebriar isqulug unleashes a cloud of toxic spores that burrow into the skin of any living nonfungus creature that is adjacent to them. The spores deal @Damage[2d6[persistent,poison]] damage, and as long as the damage persists, the creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} from the numbness caused by the spores.

Malleability.name: Malleability
Malleability.description: The isqulug can @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.kMcV8e5EZUxa6evt]{Squeeze} through tight spaces as if it were a Small creature. While Squeezing, it can move at its full Speed. The isqulug can even Squeeze through spaces that typically fit only a Tiny creature, but does so at the standard speed for Squeezing.

Tanglebriar Isqulug.name: Tanglebriar Isqulug
Tanglebriar Isqulug.publicNotes: The isqulug's appearance, though unsettling, might be its least awful aspect. The creature resembles a bipedal amphibian with tentacles instead of arms and a head composed of an undulant mass of what appear to be shifting, slimy transparent eggs filled with writhing larvae. In truth, these larvae constitute the mind and consciousness of the isqulug-its "body" is little more than an organic suit manufactured from the flesh of those it has consumed, analogous to the complex web of a spider or the hive of a colony of bees, but fully capable of movement and violence.

Illusion.name: Illusion
Illusion.description: Although it looks real enough, the truth is that this is an illusion, created via an illusory creature spell cast by one of Gorion’s assistants who hides in the back corner of the room, sustaining the spell and directing its actions. The illusion has a Perception bonus of +15 (for initiative), an AC of 25, save bonuses of +15, and it makes strikes with a +15 bonus that deal 5d4 mental damage. Unlike a typical illusory creature spell, this one doesn’t vanish the first time it’s hit or fails a saving throw thanks to the assistant’s unique talent at creating illusions for Gorion to spar against. Instead, the illusion takes damage as normal and is only destroyed once it has taken 100 damage. A @Check[will|dc:26] save disbelieves the illusion.

Desperation Vulnerability.name: Desperation Vulnerability
Desperation Vulnerability.description: Sinmolds are aware that they're in a vulnerable state as formless "newborn fiends" and are desperate to become stronger before they become prey to more powerful demons. Whenever the sinmold is in a combat encounter and ends its turn without dealing damage to another creature, the sinmold takes @Damage[3d6[mental]] damage and becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Digestion.name: Digestion
Digestion.description: The first time in a round when the sinmold damages a creature with Engulf, the sinmold immediately restores Hit Points equal to the damage dealt, gaining Hit Points in excess of its maximum as temporary Hit Points that last for 1 hour. As long as the sinmold possesses these temporary Hit Points, its surface hardens, and its AC increases to 30.

Sinmold Infestation.name: Sinmold Infestation
Sinmold Infestation.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:32]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 @Damage[2d8[poison]] damage (1 round)

Stage 2 @Damage[3d8[poison]] damage and can hear the thoughts of root rotters within 30 feet as an imprecise sense (1 round)

Stage 3 as stage 2, but @Damage[4d8[poison]] damage and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.3uh1r86TzbQvosxv]{Doomed 1} (1 round)

Stage 4 as stage 3, and arise as a root rotter upon death (1 round)

Ulugurnix.name: Ulugurnix

Draconic Frenzy.name: Draconic Frenzy
Draconic Frenzy.description: The dragon makes two claw Strikes and one horn Strike in any order.

Ghoul Whispers.name: Ghoul Whispers
Ghoul Whispers.description:
Requirements A @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.6uEgoh53GbXuHpTF]{Paralyzed}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}, or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fBnFDH2MTzgFijKf]{Unconscious} creature is within the ghoul's reach

Effect The ghoul whispers dark thoughts and vile cravings into the creature's ears. The creature must save against the forbidden cravings curse.

Forbidden Cravings (curse) A creature can still eat and drink while sickened by this curse

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:30|traits:curse], using the high spell DC for the ghoul's level

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effects (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d6[void]] damage and the target is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} until it consumes raw meat (1 day)

Stage 3 as stage 2

Stage 4 as stage 2 unless the target has consumed raw meat in the past 24 hours, then it takes @Damage[4d6[void]] damage and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} until it consumes raw meat;

Stage 5 if the creature has eaten raw meat in the past 24 hours, it dies and rises as a ghoul, if not, it returns to stage 4

Grave Knowledge.name: Grave Knowledge
Grave Knowledge.description:
Frequency once per hour

Effect The ghoul calls upon knowledge it retains from one creature it has consumed in the past 7 days. The ghoul attempts a skill check using a skill in which the consumed creature was trained (if it's unclear whether the creature was trained, the GM decides). The ghoul is treated as trained and uses a +23 modifier. This takes the same amount of actions or time as usual for the check.

The ghoul can instead automatically learn something specific known by a creature it consumed in the last 7 days, like the location of a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.iU0fEDdBp3rXpTMC]{Hidden} treasure or the name of a loved one. The ghoul can do this only once for a given creature, no matter how much of its flesh the ghoul consumed.

Twisting Tail.name: Twisting Tail
Twisting Tail.description:
Trigger A creature within reach of the dragon's tail uses a move action or leaves a square during a move action it's using

Effect The dragon makes a tail Strike at the creature with a –2 penalty. If the Strike hits, the dragon disrupts the creature's action.

Consume Flesh.name: Consume Flesh
Consume Flesh.description:
Requirements The ghoul is adjacent to the corpse of a creature that died within the last hour.

Effect The ghoul devours a chunk of the corpse and regains @Damage[6d6[healing]] Hit Points.

It can regain Hit Points from any given corpse only once.

Draconic Momentum.name: Draconic Momentum
Draconic Momentum.description: The dragon recharges their Poison Breath whenever they score a critical hit with a Strike.

Forest Passage.name: Forest Passage
Forest Passage.description: The horned dragon ignores any difficult terrain caused by plants, such as bushes, vines, and undergrowth. Even plants manipulated by magic don't impede their progress.

Impaling Charge.name: Impaling Charge
Impaling Charge.description:
Requirements The dragon doesn't have a creature impaled on their horn

Effect The dragon attempts to gore a foe. They Stride, then attempt a horn Strike. On a hit, the target becomes impaled on the dragon's horn. The creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} while on the horn (and can attempt to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.SkZAQRkLLkmBQNB9]{Escape} as normal). The dragon doesn't need to use additional actions to keep the impaled creature grabbed. If the dragon moves, they bring the grabbed creature along with them.

Ulugurnix.publicNotes:
The magic that flows through primal dragons can manifest more animalistic or bestial features in a given type of dragon. Notably among these are the massive paired horns of the horned dragon. While their bulky frames, natural coloration, and prominent ridged scales are all remarkable in their own way, it's the horns that are most obvious and striking at first glance. Horned dragons use their horns to impale their prey in a quick and brutal display of their might. They are generally contemplative and have a fixation on knowledge and self-discipline, traits belied by their bestial appearance. As a result, horned dragons are generally more open to speaking with outsiders.

Dragons come in myriad forms, with many having magical abilities or connections to magic. Some dragons draw greater power from magic than others, allowing them to manifest abilities or alter their physiques with prolonged exposure to magic. These dragons become more powerful as they age and strengthen their connections with their magical origins. Scholars debate the classification of these dragons, with some preferring the name magical dragons and others using traditional dragons due to their connection to specific magical traditions. Regardless of their names, these dragons share a number of characteristics: their ability to tap into magical energies, intensified might and cunning as they grow older, and an inclination to hoard vast amounts of treasure and wealth.

Omox.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

Cleanly Vulnerability.name: Cleanly Vulnerability
Cleanly Vulnerability.description: An omox embodies filth, and they find the concept of cleanliness abhorrent. An omox subjected to an effect that cleans them, such as the tidy command of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.Qw3fnUlaUbnn7ipC]{Prestidigitation}, takes @Damage[2d6[mental]] damage. They also take this damage the first time each round a creature hit by one of the omox's attacks spends actions cleaning off the filth.

Liquid Leap.name: Liquid Leap
Liquid Leap.description:
Requirements The omox is in a space of liquid.

Effect The omox teleports from its current space to any unoccupied space of liquid within 120 feet.

Slime Trap.name: Slime Trap
Slime Trap.description:
A creature hit by an omox's slime ball must succeed at a @Check[reflex|dc:32] save or take a –10-foot circumstance penalty to its Speeds for 1 minute or until it [[/act escape dc=35]]{Escapes (DC 35)}. On a critical failure, the creature is also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} for the same duration.

@UUID[Compendium.pf2e.bestiary-effects.Item.XSAmMuMgMvdjdpHc]{Effect: Slime Trap}

Smother.name: Smother
Smother.description:
Requirements The omox has a creature @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.VcDeM8A5oI6VqhbM]{Restrained}

Effect The demon flows over the creature, covering it in oozing acidic slime. The creature must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:32] save or it becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.XgEqL1kFApUbl5Z2]{Blinded} and must hold its breath or begin suffocating. These effects lasts as long as the omox has the creature grabbed or restrained.

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Absorb Weapon.name: Absorb Weapon
Absorb Weapon.description:
Trigger A creature hits the omox with a melee weapon

Effect The omox attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.Dt6B1slsBy8ipJu9]{Disarm} the creature. On a critical success, the weapon becomes subsumed within the omox's body rather than falling to the ground. Retrieving the weapon requires Disarming the omox of it.

Omox.name: Omox
Omox.publicNotes:
Seemingly made from living, animated filth, omoxes have no true anatomy, although they generally spend most of their time in roughly humanoid shapes, resembling some grim caricatures of half-melted humanoids. While scholars once believed these foul demons to be a pure, concentrated form of the corruption that suffuses the Outer Rifts and its inhabitants, in truth these demons arise from the souls of those who routinely befouled and polluted their surroundings in life.

When a sinful mortal soul is judged and sent on to the Outer Rifts, it can become a deadly fiend—a demon. Demons are living incarnations of sin—be they classic sins like wrath or gluttony, or more "specialized" depravities like an obsession with torture or the act of treason or treachery. Once formed, a demon's driving goals are twofold—the amassing of personal power, and the corruption of mortal souls to cause them to become tainted by sin. In this way demons ensure a never-ending supply of new demons to bolster their ever-growing ranks in the Outer Rifts.

Demons are selfish and self-absorbed creatures, and most firmly believe that mortals only play at being more virtuous than fiends. They enjoy tempting mortals into damnation to both indulge their egos and swell their armies. Like many other fiends, one of the great rewards of this manipulation is fulfilling their hunger for souls. In their eyes, the primary use for these souls is to spawn new demons, who can serve as soldiers, slaves, pawns, or even currency for their more powerful masters.

Ofalth.name: Ofalth

Filth Wallow.name: Filth Wallow
Filth Wallow.description: An ofalth gains fast healing 2 when in an area with a high concentration of debris or excrement, such as a refuse heap or sewer.

Wretched Weeps.description:
Saving Throw @Check[fortitude|dc:26]

Stage 1 carrier with no ill effect (1 day)

Stage 2 @Damage[2d4[bleed]]{2d4 persistent bleed} every hour and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 1} (1 day);

Stage 3 @Damage[2d6[bleed]]{2d6 persistent bleed} every hour and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.MIRkyAjyBeXivMa7]{Enfeebled 2} (1 day)
Wretched Weeps.name: Wretched Weeps

Refuse Pile.name: Refuse Pile
Refuse Pile.description:
When they're not in danger, an ofalth can spend 1 minute settling into a 10-foot pile that looks like a heap of garbage. Until the next time it takes an action, the ofalth gains a +2 circumstance bonus to AC.

A creature that enters the area of the garbage heap or interacts with it must attempt a save against the ofalth's stench.

Ofalth.publicNotes:
Fully grown ofalths capture victims and slowly eat them alive.

Found in castle dung heaps, city dumps, and sewers, ofalths are living amalgamations of wet detritus, sewage, and rubbish. They carry a disease called wretched weeps that causes the victim's blood to seep from its pores.

Signature Spells.name: Signature Spells
Signature Spells.description: Alzarius can cast @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.oUDNCArkQTdhllxD]{Aqueous Orb}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.SUKaxVZW2TlM8lu0]{Cleanse Affliction}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.rfZpqmj0AIIdkVIs]{Heal}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.xxWhyl81w3ckslAU]{Howling Blizzard}, and @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.kHyjQbibRGPNCixx]{Ice Storm} at a higher rank by spending a spell slot of that rank.

Snowcaster's Legacy.name: Snowcaster's Legacy
Snowcaster's Legacy.description: When Alzarius inflicts damage with a Strike, he deals an additional 2d6 cold damage as shards of ice and blasts of frozen wind slash and buffet the creature struck.

Frozen Bloodline.name: Frozen Bloodline
Frozen Bloodline.description: Alzarius's sorcerous bloodline is tied to the element of water—particularly to its manifestation in the form of ice or snow. When he casts a spell that inflicts cold damage, the target takes an additional 1 cold damage per spell rank.

Masked Lies.name: Masked Lies
Masked Lies.description: As long as Alzarius wears his Razmir mask, it's very difficult to tell if he's lying. All Perception checks to see through his deceptions take a –4 circumstance penalty as a result.

Skilled Diplomat.name: Skilled Diplomat
Skilled Diplomat.description: Whenever Alzarius attempts to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.OX4fy22hQgUHDr0q]{Make an Impression} using Diplomacy, he can attempt his check against the Will DC of up to 50 creatures at once. If he focuses on Making an Impression on just one target, he treats a success as a critical success. Finally, whenever he makes a Request, he can make requests as if the target's attitude toward him was one step better than it is, as long as they aren't hostile.

Quickened Casting.name: Quickened Casting
Quickened Casting.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect Alzarius can cast a spell more efficiently. If his next action is to cast a cantrip or a spell up to 4th-rank, he reduces the number of actions it takes to cast it by 1 (minimum 1 action).

Walder Resket.name: Walder Resket
Walder Resket.publicNotes: Although he is almost 60 years old, Walder is still fit and sharp-minded. The general is always dressed in his military uniform, and his naval hat is almost always at hand if not on his head. His hair has long gone gray, but he keeps it pulled taught and his goatee is neatly trimmed.

Joleari Underfoot.name: Joleari Underfoot
Joleari Underfoot.publicNotes:
Working to load and unload cargo from ships, dockhands are considered unruly, but many stay focused and work hard until the job is done. Some do celebrate the end of their work day with rowdy drinking.

Every day, laborers perform backbreaking physical work.

Heft Crate.name: Heft Crate
Heft Crate.description:
Requirements The dockhand is adjacent to a crate

Effect The dockhand picks up a crate and heaves it up to 15 feet. Upon landing, the crate breaks open in a @Template[burst|distance:5]. Each creature within the area takes @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]] damage (@Check[reflex|dc:13|basic] save), and the area becomes difficult terrain until cleared.

Swig.name: Swig
Swig.description:
The dockhand Interacts to either draw a bottle of @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.equipment-srd.Item.UMAXLDpI6YLSfYX1]{Alcohol} or pick up a nearby unattended bottle of alcohol and drink the whole thing.

For 1 minute, the dockhand gains a +2 item bonus to melee damage rolls and saving throws against fear, but they become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1}.

Fungalsense.name: Fungalsense
Fungalsense.description: A spore tyrannosaur in contact with fungal corruption can sense the nearby motion of anything touching the same patch of fungal corruption.

Aura of Spores.name: Aura of Spores
Aura of Spores.description: 30 feet. Creatures that start their turn in the spore tyrannosaurus's aura are in danger of inhaling the toxic spores that it constantly exudes. Creatures without the fungus or plant trait take @Damage[4d6[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:30|basic] save) upon entering the aura or starting their turn in the aura. Those who fail are also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} by the spores.

Fungal Empowerment.name: Fungal Empowerment
Fungal Empowerment.description: While the spore tyrannosaurus is touching fungal corruption, it gains fast healing 10 and is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened}; it can use the extra action to Stride or Strike.

Fling.name: Fling
Fling.description:
Requirements A creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed} in the tyrannosaurus's jaws

Effect The tyrannosaurus flings the creature into the air up to 10 feet up from its mouth and 20 feet away. The creature falls 25 feet (assuming the tyrannosaurus flings it as high as it can) and takes falling damage accordingly. If the flung creature lands on another creature, the creature it lands on takes the same amount of bludgeoning damage. The creature being landed on can attempt a @Check[reflex|dc:33|basic] save.

Pin Prey.name: Pin Prey
Pin Prey.description:
Trigger The tyrannosaurus critically hits a Large or smaller foe with its foot

Effect The creature struck by the foot is knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone} and held in place. As long as the tyrannosaurus doesn't move from its position, the pinned creature is @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.kWc1fhmv9LBiTuei]{Grabbed}.

A tyrannosaurus gains a +2 circumstance bonus to attack a creature it has pinned in this manner but can only Swallow Whole if that creature is grabbed with its jaws.

Spore Breath.name: Spore Breath
Spore Breath.description: The spore tyrannosaurus unleashes a @Template[type:cone|distance:60] of highly toxic spores from its maw. Creatures in the area take @Damage[14d6[poison]] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:33|basic] save). Those who fail are also @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 1} (or @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.fesd1n5eVhpCSS18]{Sickened 2} on a critical failure). The fungal tyrannosaurus can't use the spore breath weapon again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge the spore breath weapon]]{1d4 rounds}.

Spore Tyrannosaurus.name: Spore Tyrannosaurus
Spore Tyrannosaurus.publicNotes:
Widely regarded as the king of the dinosaurs, the tyrannosaurus is a massive predator with a wide mouth filled with viciously sharp teeth. Some tribes of giants have even trained tyrannosauruses as mounts or beasts of war.

Remnants from the world's primeval era, these enormous reptilian animals still exist in large numbers in remote wildernesses or underground in magical Darklands caverns. Lizardfolk, orcs, giants, and other humanoids who live near dinosaurs use the animals as mounts, guards, or hunting beasts. Occasionally, rich nobles will collect dinosaurs to display them in menageries, which almost inevitably leads to cast-offs being nursed back to health by druids and other champions of nature. When dinosaurs establish themselves in regions outside their normal habitats, it's often the result of a large collection being released.

Otherworldly Will.name: Otherworldly Will
Otherworldly Will.description: The rotting cultist is driven forward by a singular, otherworldly will, guiding their actions. Whenever the rotting cultist attempts a Will saving throw against a mental effect that would control or dictate its actions, the rotting cultist treats the result of the saving throw as one category better.

Fungal Fervor.name: Fungal Fervor
Fungal Fervor.description:
Trigger The rotting cultist is reduced to 0 HP

Effect The rotting cultist avoids death and reduces their HP to 1. They are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1}, and each time they use this ability, their slowed value increases by 1, up to a maximum of 3. Each time they use this ability, a bloom of fungus erupts from their flesh as their movements become even more disjointed. This slowed condition is reduced by 1 each day. Note that since this is a reaction, any further damage done to a rotting cultist that reduces them to 0 HP before they regain their reactions kills them.

Sneak Attack.name: Sneak Attack
Sneak Attack.description: The rotting cultist deals an extra 2d6 precision damage to @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} creatures.

Surprise Attack.name: Surprise Attack
Surprise Attack.description: On the first round of combat, creatures that haven't acted yet are @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard} to the rotting cultist.

Pray to the Rotting God.name: Pray to the Rotting God
Pray to the Rotting God.description:
Frequency once per day

Effect The rotting cultist calls out to the Rotting God, offering up their flesh in exchange for power. The rotting cultist is healed @Damage[(4d6+8)[healing]] HP, gains a +1 status bonus on attack rolls for 1 minute, and they reduce any condition (other than slowed) affecting them by 1 (if they have a numerical value; this has no effect on conditions without values). The rotting cultist becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.xYTAsEpcJE1Ccni3]{Slowed 1} for 10 minutes as a fungal bloom erupts from their flesh.

Infesting Exhalation.name: Infesting Exhalation
Infesting Exhalation.description: The eshmok exhales a wave of stinging fiendish wasps out in a @Template[type:cone|distance:30], dealing @Damage[4d8[poison]] damage to every creature within the cone (@Check[reflex|dc:28|basic] save). The swarming fiend wasps linger in the area for 6 rounds or until the eshmok is able to use Infesting Exhalation again, whichever comes first. Each creature damaged by Infesting Exhalation or that enters the area must succeed at a @Check[fortitude|dc:28] save or take @Damage[2d8[persistent,poison]] damage and become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.i3OJZU2nk64Df3xm]{Clumsy 1} as the poison renders them dizzy and nauseous. At the end of each of their turns, they can attempt a new Fortitude save to end the effects. The eshmok can't use Infesting Exhalation again for [[/gmr 1d6 #Recharge Infesting Exhalation]]{1d6 rounds}.

Change Shape.name: Change Shape
Change Shape.description:
The eshmok turns into their fungus form or back into their normal humanoid wasp form. In fungus form, they lose their fly Speed and can't make stinger Strikes. In wasp form, they gain a tendril melee Strike (+21 for 2d8+9 slashing plus eshmok infection); the tendril strike has the agile, magical, reach 10 feet, and unholy traits.

@Localize[PF2E.NPC.Abilities.Glossary.ChangeShape]

+1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic.name: +1 Status to All Saves vs. Magic

Harmony Vulnerability.name: Harmony Vulnerability
Harmony Vulnerability.description: An eshmok's wrathful infestations defines them, and forcing peace upon them wrenches at their soul. If they fail a save against calm or a similar effect forcing them to be peaceful, an eshmok takes @Damage[4d6[mental]] damage.

Eshmok Infection.name: Eshmok Infection
Eshmok Infection.description:
A creature that's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.nlCjDvLMf2EkV2dl]{Quickened} by eshmok infection can use the extra action each round for only Strike actions. A creature that's @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.yblD8fOR1J8rDwEQ]{Confused} by eshmok infection never considers an eshmok in fungal form as a target

Saving Throw @Check[will|dc:28]

Maximum Duration 6 rounds

Stage 1 confused (1 round)

Stage 2 confused and quickened (1 round)

Stage 3 confused, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}, and quickened (1 round)

Eshmok.name: Eshmok
Eshmok.publicNotes:
Eshmoks are proof that anger consumes a creature. Formed from wrathful souls, these demons resemble giant humanoid wasps who have fallen victim to parasitic fungi. The fungi's foul-looking fibrous material is a physical manifestation of wrath. Tendrils of it burst from eshmok bodies, emitting rage-inducing spores, while lattices of nest-like growths from their torsos shelter wasplike infestations.

Wrathful Parasites

The swarms that infest an eshmok aren't its allies, but incarnations of anger that serve to constantly harry and agonize the creature. Some maintain that these wasps are manifestations of Calistria's vengeance, but her faithful believe something closer to the truth—that these wasps represent a mockery of vengeance and a corruption of the directed rage their goddess teaches and epitomizes. Eshmoks are particularly reviled by worshipers of Calistria as a result.
Eshmok.allSaves: +1 status to all saves vs. magic

equipment-Cold Iron Arrows.name: Cold Iron Arrows
equipment-Cold Iron Arrows.description: These projectiles are the ammunition for bows. The shaft of an arrow is made of wood. It is stabilized in flight by fletching at one end and bears a metal head on the other.

Counterspell.name: Counterspell
Counterspell.description:
Trigger A creature Casts a Spell that Delvarnis knows

Effect Delvarnis expends a spell slot of the same level and then attempts to counteract the triggering spell with a [[/gmr 1d20+18 #Counteract]]{+18} bonus on the check.

Otherworldly Will.description: Delvarnis is driven forward by a singular, otherworldly will, guiding their actions. Whenever Delvarnis attempts a Will saving throw against a mental effect that would control or dictate their actions, Delvarnis treats the result of the saving throw as one category better.
Otherworldly Will.name: Otherworldly Will

Unexplained Demise.name: Unexplained Demise
Unexplained Demise.description:
Trigger Delvarnis is captured alive

Effect Blood pours from Delvarnis' ears and nose, and they drop dead on the spot. An adjacent PC who witnesses this unexplained death must succeed at a @Check[will|dc:27] save or become @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Razmir's Disappointment.name: Razmir's Disappointment
Razmir's Disappointment.description: Delvarnis inflicts an additional 4d6 mental damage with melee Strikes made while he wears a mask. On a critical hit with such a Strike, the creature struck becomes @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.TBSHQspnbcqxsmjL]{Frightened 1}.

Steady Spellcasting.name: Steady Spellcasting
Steady Spellcasting.description: If a reaction would disrupt Delvarnis's spellcasting action, he attempts a @Check[flat|dc:15]. If he succeeds, his action isn't disrupted.

equipment-+2 Striking Staff of Control (.name: +2 Striking Staff of Control (Greater)
equipment-+2 Striking Staff of Control (.description:
An array of dazzling gemstones lines the twisting head of the golden staff. While wielding the staff, you gain a +1 status bonus to Diplomacy checks to make a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.actionspf2e.Item.DCb62iCBrJXy0Ik6]{Request}.

Activate Cast a Spell

Effect You expend a number of charges from the staff to cast a spell from its list.

  • Cantrip @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4gBIw4IDrSfFHik4]{Daze}
  • 1st @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.aIHY2DArKFweIrpf]{Command}
  • 2nd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.tlSE7Ly8vi1Dgddv]{Laughing Fit}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.CQb8HtQ1BPeZmu9h]{Stupefy}
  • 3rd @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.IihxWhRfpsBgQ5jS]{Enthrall}
  • 4th @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.vLA0q0WOK2YPuJs6]{Charm}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.LiGbewa9pO0yjbsY]{Confusion}, @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.qwlh6aDgi86U3Q7H]{Suggestion}

Craft Requirements Supply one casting of all listed ranks of all listed spells.

equipment-Demon Mask (Greater, Appears a.name: Demon Mask (Greater, Appears as a Mask of Razmir)
equipment-Demon Mask (Greater, Appears a.description:
This terrifying mask is crafted in the visage of a leering demon and grants a +2 item bonus to Intimidation checks.

Activate—Leering Mask 2 (manipulate)

Frequency once per day

Effect The mask casts a 3rd-rank @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.spells-srd.Item.4koZzrnMXhhosn0D]{Fear} spell with a DC of 29.
